extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of classical Athenian history; scholars of ancient Greek political institutions
extracted.subtask_description: Descriptive rules and procedures governing Athenian citizenship, magistracies, assemblies, and administrative offices (composition, selection, duties, penalties, and processes) as recorded in a classical historical/constitutional account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms of reconciliation and secession at Eleusis
rubrics_metrics.description: All persons who remained in the city but wished to leave might settle at Eleusis retaining civil rights and full self-government; the temple at Eleusis to be common ground under Ceryces and Eumolpidae; settlers barred from entering Athens except during the mysteries; secessionists to pay their share for common defence; house purchase disputes decided by three valuers on each side; list of seceders to be made within ten days and departure within twenty; persons out of country get same terms on return; seceders not eligible for Athenian office until re-registration; homicide trials to follow ancestral practice; general amnesty for past events except specified officers unless they submit accounts appropriately; each party repays its war-borrowings separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies timing, property-dispute procedure (valuers), limits on political participation for seceders, exceptions to amnesty, and financial settlement responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Franchise and citizen enrollment procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Franchise open only to those of citizen birth by both parents; enrolled among demesmen at eighteen; demesmen assess age and parentage on oath and can dismiss underage or non-free-born candidates; appeal to law-courts if declared not free-born; Council examines enrollments and may fine demesmen for enrolling underage youths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes appeal mechanism (accusers appointed by demesmen), punishment for wrongful enrollment (sale as slave if appeal lost), and Council oversight/fines for demesmen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and military initiation of youths (Ephebi)
rubrics_metrics.description: After enrollment, fathers appoint three tribe-elders over forty as guardians (one elected by Assembly), plus a director; youths make circuit of temples, garrison Piraeus/Munichia, receive trainers for heavy armour, bow, javelin and catapult; guardians receive a drachma and youths four obols; first year communal provisions and supervision, second year public display, receive shield and spear, patrol country and serve in forts, are exempt from taxes and from bringing/being subject to civil actions (with specified exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies durations, allowances, exemptions from litigation, and the sequence of military training and civic duties for the two-year period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of ordinary magistrates and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: All magistrates concerned with ordinary administration are elected by lot, with exceptions: Military Treasurer, Commissioners of the Theoric fund, Superintendent of Springs are elected by vote; all military officers are elected by vote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes between offices by lot (random selection) and those by vote (electoral selection); terms run from one Panathenaic festival to the next for elected-by-vote officers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council of Five Hundred composition and basic role
rubrics_metrics.description: Council of Five Hundred elected by lot—fifty members from each tribe; each tribe holds the office of Prytanes in turn; Council convened daily (unless holiday), preliminary cognizance of matters for Assembly, inspects public works and triremes, shares duties with other magistrates, examines candidates for its own membership and the nine Archons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council prepares programme for Council and Assembly sessions, takes preliminary view of matters before the Assembly may vote, and can report suspected fraud to the Assembly and law-courts; its judgments are generally not final and are subject to appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prytanes rotation, duties and prytany structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Each tribe's Prytanes serve in turn; first four prytanies serve 36 days, last six 35 (lunar reckoning). Prytanes mess together in the Tholus, receive state maintenance, convene Council and Assembly meetings, produce the programme of business, and decide subject scheduling and sittings. They arrange four Assembly meetings each prytany with specified purposes (sovereign Assembly, petitions, hearing of certain categories, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One meeting per prytany is 'sovereign' for ratifying magistrates, considering corn supply and defense, introducing impeachments, reading property lists and inheritances; the sixth prytany considers ostracism and accepts certain complaints; laws require treatment of three religious, three herald/embassy, and three secular questions across meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: President of the Prytanes: role and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: A single President of the Prytanes is elected by lot to preside for one night and one day only; may not hold office twice; keeps keys of sanctuaries, public records and the public seal; must remain in the Tholus with one-third of the Prytanes; appoints nine Proedri by lot (one from each tribe except the current Prytanes') who conduct meetings, preserve order, present subjects, decide voting results and may dismiss meetings; one Proedri is appointed President of the meeting. No one may be President more than once per year; a man may be Proedrus once per prytany.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits on tenure prevent concentration of authority; functions emphasize custody of records/treasures and procedural control of meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly meeting prerequisites and illegal proposal risk
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assembly cannot vote on a question unless it has first been considered by the Council and placed on the programme by the Prytanes; a person who carries a motion in the Assembly without following these procedures is liable to an action for illegal proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes a formal gatekeeping function on the Council and Prytanes to structure Assembly business and provides legal accountability for bypassing the procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sovereign Assembly responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'sovereign' Assembly meeting in each prytany must ratify continuance of magistrates if performing duties, consider supply of corn and defense, receive impeachments, read lists of confiscated property and applications for inheritance and wards of state so nothing passes unclaimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designates a recurring Assembly session for oversight of magistrates, financial supply, legal notifications and introduction of charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elections for generals and other military commanders
rubrics_metrics.description: Elections to offices of General and Hipparch and other military commands are held in the Assembly in such manner as the people decide; they are held after the sixth prytany by the first board of Prytanes in whose term the omens are favourable, with a preliminary consideration by the Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines popular election timing, religious/omen considerations, and Council vetting before election.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on Council judicial penalties and appeals to law-courts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council formerly had power to inflict fines, imprisonment and death, but after abuses the people removed these powers; if the Council condemns or inflicts a fine, the Thesmothetae must bring the sentence before the law-court and the jurors' decision is final. Private individuals may bring information against magistrates, with appeal to law-courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies separation between preliminary Council judgement and final judicial authority residing in law-courts; provides appeal route and finality of jury decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council oversight of naval construction and master-builders
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council supervises triremes and their tackle/sheds and builds new triremes or quadriremes as the Assembly votes; Assembly appoints master-builders by vote; Council appoints ten commissioners chosen from its members to oversee shipbuilding; if master-builders fail to hand over completed ships the old Council cannot receive its customary donation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details division of responsibilities between Assembly (authorisation and appointment) and Council (oversight and commissioners), with financial incentives tied to timely completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration of public contracts and leases (Poletae)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ten Commissioners for Public Contracts (Poletae), one from each tribe chosen by lot, farm out public contracts, lease mines and taxes in conjunction with Military Treasurer and Commissioners of Theoric fund, sell confiscated property, hand over lists of farmed taxes on whitened tablets with instalment schedules and maintain lists for various prytanies and instalment timings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies record-keeping (whitened tablets), durations for leases (workable mines three years, sacred enclosures ten years with instalment schedules), and procedures for sale and payment terms (farms 10 years, dwellings 5 years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Receivers-General duties in revenue collection and apportionment
rubrics_metrics.description: Ten Receivers-General (Apodectae), one from each tribe elected by lot, receive the tablets and strike off instalments as paid in the Council's presence, note defaulters (liable to double payment or imprisonment), receive instalments on one day and apportion funds among magistrates, then publicly present the apportionment and invite accusations of malpractice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines cash-handling, enforcement of payment penalties, transparent reporting of apportionments, and a mechanism for public accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit and examination of magistrates' accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council elects ten Auditors (Logistae) by lot to audit magistrates for each prytany and one Examiner of Accounts (Euthunus) by lot from each tribe with two assessors; within three days of audit passing, any one may record a charge on a whitened tablet naming himself and the magistrate and alleged malpractice and requested penalty; the Examiner forwards private cases to local justices and public cases to Thesmothetae who may bring accounts before the law-court; final judgement rests with jurors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details timelines, filing format (whitened tablets), procedural routing for private vs public charges, and the role of Thesmothetae in lodging cases to the courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cavalry enrollment and horse inspection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council inspects state horses: owners keeping good horses in bad condition are mulcted in corn allowance; horses unable to keep up or that shy are branded with a wheel on the jaw and disqualified for service; Council inspects recruits for scouts and disqualifies unfit individuals, depriving them of horse/payscale; Commissioners of Enrolment (Catalogeis) draw up cavalry roll by open vote and hand list to Hipparchs and Phylarchs who present candidates to Council for final suitability vote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies physical and behavioural fitness standards for horses and riders, penalties for poor maintenance, the enrollment process and voting for suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer of public building decisions to juries
rubrics_metrics.description: Formerly the Council decided plans for public buildings and robe-making for Athena, but because of perceived favouritism this work is now done by a jury in law-courts appointed by lot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates a procedural reform moving procurement/contract decisions from Council discretion to jury adjudication to reduce favouritism.

rubrics_metrics.name: State support for infirm paupers
rubrics_metrics.description: Law provides that persons possessing less than three minas who are so crippled as to be unable to work, after examination by the Council, receive two obols a day from the state; a treasurer is appointed by lot to attend to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines an eligibility monetary threshold, medical/physical examination by Council, fixed relief amount, and appointed administrative oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temple repairs commissioners' funding and duty
rubrics_metrics.description: Ten Commissioners for Repairs of Temples, elected by lot, receive thirty minas from the Receivers-General to carry out the most necessary temple repairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies composition, funding source, and restricted spending purpose (necessary repairs).

rubrics_metrics.name: City Commissioners (Astynomi) urban regulation duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Ten City Commissioners (five for Piraeus and five for the city) ensure female entertainers are not hired at more than two drachmas (lot used if multiple hirers), prevent sewage discharge within ten stradia of walls, forbid street-blocking by building or barriers, regulate door-opening directions and remove corpses from streets using a body of state slaves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers regulation of hiring rates for entertainers, public health/sewage rules, urban planning obstructions, and public sanitation responsibilities including use of state slaves for corpse removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market Commissioners (Agoranomi) duty to ensure purity
rubrics_metrics.description: Market Commissioners, elected by lot (five for Piraeus and five for the city), are statutorily duty-bound to ensure that all articles offered for sale in the market are pure and unadulterated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates inspection and enforcement against adulteration of goods in markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioners of Weights and Measures (Metronomi) enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Metronomi, five for city and five for Piraeus elected by lot, ensure sellers use fair weights and measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies standardisation/enforcement role to protect fair commerce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corn Commissioners (Sitophylaces) responsibilities for grain pricing and weights
rubrics_metrics.description: Sitophylaces (formerly ten, now twenty for city and fifteen for Piraeus) ensure unprepared corn in the market is offered at reasonable prices, millers sell barley meal at price proportionate to barley, bakers sell loaves at price proportionate to wheat and of a weight the Commissioners appoint; law requires them to fix standard loaves' weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes price-proportion rules, standardisation of baked goods, and increases in number of commissioners to meet administrative needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Superintendents of the Mart duty to ensure corn supply
rubrics_metrics.description: Ten Superintendents of the Mart, elected by lot, superintend the Mart and compel merchants to bring into the city two-thirds of the corn brought by sea to the Corn Mart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigns responsibility for urban food supply logistics and a quota for market availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Eleven's responsibility for prisoners and execution procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Eleven, appointed by lot, care for prisoners in the state gaol; thieves, kidnappers and pickpockets are brought to them and if they plead guilty they are executed; if they deny the charge the Eleven bring the case before the law-courts; if acquitted they are released, if convicted the Eleven execute them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies custody, preliminary disposition based on plea, referral to courts for contested cases, and authority to carry out sentences following court outcomes.
